subject: Post-call: pricing path & participation options for TinyHealth
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ana Torres <ana@tinyhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: pricing path & participation options for TinyHealth

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and suggested next steps so we don’t lose momentum. High-level notes from the call: 

- Primary use case: clinical triage assistant for patient intake; peak generation mostly short prompts but regular multi-turn context (avg seq ~600 tokens).
- Current pilot target: 100M tokens/month initially, scale to 300–500M over 6–12 months if latency and accuracy meet expectations.
- Procurement ask: target blended cost that keeps infra spend under $4k–$6k / month initially (TinyHealth finance), they also asked about $/1M token target for planning (they threw out ~$600/1M tokens as a mental anchor).

Paths we discussed: 1) Redwood Starter (startup credits + founder credit) for the first 3–6 months; 2) Committed-use (1yr) for a predictable base rate; 3) Multi-year (2yr) for additional step-downs.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short summary of the Starter terms (redwood-starter-terms.pdf) and a pricing workbook we can use to model their expected burn.

Immediate asks / proposed next steps:
- Ana / procurement: confirm a realistic monthly budget band you can commit to for the pilot (range is fine — e.g. $3k–$6k / month or higher).
- TinyHealth: confirm whether you prefer a short paid trial (6 weeks) or a 1–3 month pilot with a guaranteed minimum commit.
- Redwood (Ben / Marissa): we’ll run unit-econ examples ($/1M tokens) for the three paths and get back with a recommended starter proposal and any founder credit we can apply.

If that summary looks right I’ll follow up with concrete $/1M token scenarios and a proposed 6-week trial SOW.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

From: Ana Torres <ana@tinyhealth.ai>

Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:03:10 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: pricing path & participation options for TinyHealth

Thanks Soojin — that recap is spot on. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The $3k–$6k / month band is the finance team's comfort zone for the very first month of pilot spend. If we see results, we can expand.
- The $600/1M tokens number was a rough target the CTO used to sanity-check potential vendors — it’s not a firm ask, just context.
- We want to understand what starter credits look like in practice (how long they last, and whether they stack with a short-term committed discount).
- Multi-year is interesting only if we can get a meaningful step-down vs 1yr committed.

Procurement: Marco / team, are you able to review a short SOW + 6-week trial with a small credit? We can loop legal after we see a draft.

Quick Qs for Redwood: can you show two example blended $/1M scenarios (starter path vs 1yr committed) with the 100M and 300M token/month profiles? Also, any limits on KV cache or autoscaling we should know about for pilot throughput?

—Ana
Ana Torres
Head of Product, TinyHealth
ana@tinyhealth.ai | +1 (212) 555-4420

Subject: Re: Post-call: pricing path & participation options for TinyHealth

Ana — thanks for the quick reply and the context. Below are two worked examples so you can see unit economics for the pilot profiles you mentioned. These are illustrative blended $/1M token numbers, including applicable starter credits / discounts: 

Scenario A — Starter path (short trial + founder credit):
- Pilot: 100M tokens / month
- Starter credits: one-time founder credit covering first 100M tokens (~100% of month 1) + 30% off for months 2–3 (starter program).
- Blended $/1M tokens (month-1 weighted): roughly $420–$480 / 1M tokens over the first 3 months depending on usage distribution.

Scenario B — Committed-use path (1yr commit, standard reserve):
- Pilot scale: guarantee 100M tokens/month for 12 months with monthly true-ups.
- Discount: baseline 20% off list for 1yr commit; possible additional 5–10% performance rebate tied to volume milestones.
- Blended $/1M tokens: roughly $520–$650 / 1M tokens in early months, trending lower as volume ramps.

Notes on multi-year: a 2yr committed contract typically buys an extra 7–10% off the 1yr baseline in our standard packaging; economics only beat Starter if you expect steady traffic beyond month 6.

Autoscaling/KV cache: For your average seq length (~600) and expected throughput, our runtime supports continuous batching and prefix caching that should keep p50 latency in the 120–220ms range for synchronous requests at the 100M/mo profile. I’ll have engineering confirm the cache limits for your model variant but no hard blocker expected.

Attachments: I’ve attached a simple pricing workbook with the math broken out (pricing-workbook.xlsx) so you can share with finance.

Suggested next steps: 
1) If you prefer the Starter+trial approach, we propose a 6-week paid trial: Redwood provides a founder credit covering the first 100M tokens, then standard starter discounts for months 2–3.
2) If Procurement wants predictability, we can draft a 1yr committed quote with a 20% base discount and tiered rebates as volume milestones are hit.
3) I’ll draft both options (SOW + short pricing appendix) and share a DocuSign link for whichever path you pick.

If you want a one-pager comparing total spend at 100M vs 300M tokens over 6 months, say the word and I’ll drop it into the workbook.

Best,
Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachment: pricing-workbook.xlsx
